children: The annual inflation rate in Bosnia and Herzegovina rose to 4.9% in August 2026 from 3.6% in the previous month, marking the highest reading in three months.
Price growth accelerated for alcoholic beverages and tobacco (3.9% vs 3.0% in July), housing and utilities (11.3% vs 10.8%), transport (22.9% vs 13.0%), and recreation and culture (3.9% vs 3.6%).
Conversely, inflation eased for furnishings, household equipment, and routine maintenance (1.9% vs 2.8%), health (5.5% vs 5.9%), and other goods and services (1.4% vs 1.6%).

Inflation was unchanged for communication (3.1%), education (1.8%), and restaurants and hotels (4.8%), while deflation eased for food and non-alcoholic beverages (-0.9% vs -1.1%) but deepened for clothing and footwear (-8.7% vs -7.9%).
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 1.1% in August, rebounding from a 0.4% fall in July, ending a three-month streak of monthly deflation.

title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Inflation at 3-Month High
